title: I-O Interface Functions
body:
The five jobs an [[I-O Interface]] is there to do:

- **Error detection**, parity and framing errors on the way in
- **Communication with the [[CPU]]**, decoding addresses off the [[System Bus]] and
  responding as a memory location under [[Memory Mapping]]
- **Data [[Buffering]]**, because the device and the CPU do not run at the same speed
- **Allow the CPU to control the I/O operation**, via the [[Control Register]]
- **Allow the CPU to monitor I/O status**, via the [[Status Register]]

Everything the interface does is one of those five, which is a useful check when a design
question asks what belongs in the interface and what belongs in the driver.
